headline: Equipment and franchise growth lift margins y/y
summary_short: Planet Fitness's Q1 FY2026 revenue was $337.2M, up 21.9% y/y (down 10.4% q/q on Q4 seasonality), with net income up 23.1% y/y to $51.6M ($0.65 diluted EPS) even as interest expense rose 25.8% y/y and stockholders' equity stayed deeply negative at -$482.2M after continued share buybacks.
summary_long: Revenue growth was led by equipment (+123.4% y/y to $62.1M on higher franchisee orders) and franchise (+16.7% y/y, including a NAF revenue jump from a 1%-point rate increase), while corporate-owned clubs grew a slower 5.2%, weighed by 8 California clubs sold to a franchisee in 2025. System-wide same club sales rose 3.5%. Operating margin expanded to 29.3% from 28.7%. Interest expense rose 25.8% y/y on a higher note balance following December 2025's issuance. The company repurchased $51.1M of stock in the quarter, holding equity at -$482.2M. Cash rose to $375.3M on $147.5M of operating cash flow. No forward guidance was stated.

drivers.explanation: Total revenue rose 21.9% y/y to $337.2 million driven by growth across all three segments, most sharply in equipment sales to franchisees.

Equipment segment revenue rose 123.4% y/y ($34.3M) on higher replacement and new-club equipment sales to franchisee-owned clubs; franchise segment revenue rose 16.7% partly from a 1%-point NAF contribution rate increase.
Operating margin expanded to 29.3% from 28.7% as total operating costs grew only to 70.7% of revenue from 71.3%, per the MD&A's expense table.
Cost of revenue, which relates primarily to the equipment segment, rose 101.6% y/y in line with higher equipment sales volumes to franchisee-owned clubs.
Higher operating income drove the 23.1% y/y net income gain, partially offset by $6.8 million more interest expense from the December 2025 note issuance.
Capital expenditures rose to $25.5 million from $23.1 million, mainly from higher spending on existing corporate-owned clubs ($16.2M vs $11.7M).
Equity stayed deeply negative at -$482.2 million, reflecting $51.1 million of Q1 share repurchases and retirements against the company's leveraged capital structure.
Cash rose on $147.5 million of operating cash flow, including a $39.2 million working-capital inflow, exceeding $47.2 million of investing outflows and $55.6 million of financing outflows.
